flagged.title: Commonwealth migration after 1945
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims the British Nationality Act was passed weeks before the Windrush arrived (F10) and attributes the concept of patriality and making passport holders stateless to the 1968 Act (F13), both of which teach incorrect legal definitions and historical chronology.

mark_affecting.quote: Just weeks before the Windrush arrived, the government passed the 1948 British Nationality Act. Basically, this act confirmed that all Commonwealth subjects were officially British citizens.
a crucial exam term that was introduced by that 1968 Act, and that's patriality... the 1968 Act effectively made them stateless overnight.

flagged.title: Ideas of Englishness and Britishness over time
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Norman migrants assimilated rapidly within a few generations and anglicised their names, which misteaches a key medieval case study on change and continuity.

mark_affecting.quote: Groups from your early lessons, like the Norman migrants or the Huguenot refugees, assimilated quite rapidly. Within a few generations, they anglicised their names and dissolved completely into English society.
